title: The Hey-Hay Club and the Lazia story
summary: Interviewer relates a gangster story from Jesse Price; Smith had not heard it and says trouble came mostly from outside gangsters.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: I've got a note here that there was a club in Kansas City called the Hey-Hay Club?
That's a new one on me.
Fourth and Cherry Blossom. I don't know that.

And Jesse Price, who was a drummer, he was working there. And there was a gangster named Johnny Lazia, and he got killed or something. There was some question about the musicians wanting to quit the gig. And the guys who killed Lazia herded them all into a car, along with the guys who were running the club, and they went out to somewhere outside Kansas City, and they made the musicians watch while they machine-gunned these other guys who had been running the club.
No, I didn't hear about that.

[See Jazz Style, p.22. "About dawn one day, shortly after the machine gunning of Johnny Lazia, the musicians were ordered into a large automobile by armed gangsters and driven to a lonely spot on Cliff Drive overlooking the city. There they were forced to watch a savage beating administered with sticks and junior league baseball bats to a racketeer named Nugent Lafuma. Price could only believe that the musicians were deliberately involved in the incident to impress upon them the naked power wielded by the owners of the Hey-Hay Club, a well-known Black Hand hangout, and also that discretion was demanded of them by their employers. Lafuma left town a battered wreck and dropped out of sight. The musicians returned to work and played the job the following night as if nothing had happened and the incident was never referred to again."]
Was there much of that kind of thing going on? I mean, was there a lot of shooting going on and...?

Well, a little bit when I was around there. Just a very little bit of it. But mostly it was fellows that came from there out of town, gangsters coming from out of town coming there... In other words...
Yeah. Trying to muscle in on the territory. That's where this stuff would come up.
